t.6.31.1: Then, having seen omens there, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with good fortune.
t.6.31.2: Securing cool water and forests rich in fruit, let us divide this vast flood of troops, draw it up in battle array, and take our stand, O Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.31.3: I see a terrible danger at hand that will bring about the destruction of the worlds, the slaughter of the foremost heroes among bears, monkeys and rākṣasas.
t.6.31.4: The winds blow harshly and the earth trembles; the peaks of the hills quiver and the mountains, bearers of the earth, are falling.
t.6.31.5: Clouds resembling flesh-eating demons, harsh and harsh-sounding, cruel, are cruelly raining down a shower mixed with drops of blood.
t.6.31.6: The twilight, resembling red sandalwood, is exceedingly dreadful, and this blazing disc of fire is falling from the sun.
t.6.31.7: Wretched, inauspicious and dreadful beasts and birds, crying out in mournful voices, howl toward the sun, engendering great fear.
t.6.31.8: And at night the moon, without its light and fringed with black and red rays, scorches the world, as it does at the destruction of the world.
t.6.31.9: A halo, small, harsh, inauspicious and deep red, and a dark blue mark are seen on the disc of the sun, O Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.31.10: The stars are not seen as they should be, and all goes on as though it were proclaiming the end of the age for the world. Look, Lakṣmaṇa!
t.6.31.12: Surrounded on all sides by the monkeys, let us swiftly march today, with all speed, against the city protected by Rāvaṇa, which is hard to assail.
t.6.31.11: Crows, hawks and vultures fly about low overhead, and jackals too utter inauspicious, loud-sounding cries.
t.6.31.13: Speaking thus to Lakṣmaṇa, the heroic elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, mighty in strength, swiftly descended from that mountain peak.
t.6.31.14: Having descended from that mountain, the righteous-souled Rāghava beheld his own army, utterly unassailable by enemies.
t.6.31.15: Then Rāghava, who knew the right moment, together with Sugrīva, made ready the great army of the monkey-king and at the proper time urged it on to battle.
t.6.31.16: Then, at the proper time, the mighty-armed bowman, surrounded by a great army, set out in the lead, facing toward the city of Laṅkā.
t.6.31.17: Then Vibhīṣaṇa and Sugrīva, Hanumān, Jāmbavān and Nala, the king of the bears, and likewise Nīla and Lakṣmaṇa followed him.
t.6.31.18: Then, behind him, the very great army of bears and forest-dwelling monkeys followed Rāghava, covering a vast expanse of the earth.
t.6.31.19: The monkeys, resembling elephants and able to hold back their foes, seized hundreds of mountain peaks and full-grown trees.
t.6.31.20: Then, in no long time, the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, subduers of their foes, reached Laṅkā, the city of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.31.22: Urged on by Rāma's words, the forest-dwellers pressed in close around that city, unassailable even by the gods, and took up their positions as they had been instructed.
t.6.31.21: Garlanded with banners, delightful, adorned with gardens and groves, with wondrous ramparts, exceedingly hard to reach, and with lofty walls and gateways.
t.6.31.23: But the northern gate of Laṅkā, lofty like a mountain peak, Rāma, bow in hand, together with his younger brother, both guarded and blockaded.
t.6.31.24: And the heroic Rāma, son of Daśaratha, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, has encamped before Laṅkā, the city guarded by Rāvaṇa.
t.6.31.25: Having reached the northern gate where Rāvaṇa stands, Rāma must take his place there, for none other than Rāma is able to guard that gate.
t.6.31.27: He saw many and varied masses of weapons belonging to the warriors, laid out in array, and likewise their coats of mail.
t.6.31.26: The two, bearing their weapons, beheld it: terrible, ruled over by Rāvaṇa as the ocean is by Varuṇa, guarded on every side by fearsome rākṣasas, and striking terror into the weak like Pātāla guarded by the Dānavas.
t.6.31.29: The exceedingly mighty Aṅgada seized the southern gate, together with Ṛṣabha, Gavākṣa, Gaja and Gavaya.
t.6.31.28: Nīla, the valiant commander of the monkey army, first reached the gate and took his stand there together with Mainda and Dvivida.
t.6.31.30: The mighty monkey Hanūmān guarded the western gate, joined by Pramāthin and Praghasa and by other heroes.
t.6.31.31: And in the central division Sugrīva himself took his stand, together with all the foremost of the monkeys, who were like Suparṇa and the wind.
t.6.31.32: Thirty-six crores of monkeys, renowned leaders of troops, have pressed close together and encamped there where the monkey Sugrīva is.
t.6.31.33: At the command of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa together with Vibhīṣaṇa stationed a koṭi of monkeys at each and every gate.
t.6.31.34: To the west of Rāma, not far off, Sugrīva stood together with Jāmbavān in the central division, followed by a large force.
t.6.31.36: All of them had misshapen tails, all bore fangs and claws as their weapons; all had bodies strangely formed and variegated, and all had grotesque faces.
t.6.31.35: But those tigers among monkeys, like fanged tigers, seized the tops of trees and mountains and stood joyfully ready for battle.
t.6.31.37: Some had the strength of ten elephants, some were ten times stronger still, and some were equal in prowess to a thousand elephants.
t.6.31.39: Wondrous and varied was their gathering; there the surging forth of the monkey hosts was like the rising of a swarm of locusts.
t.6.31.38: Some possess strength like a mighty flood, and some are a hundredfold stronger still; and others there were, leaders of the monkey troops, of immeasurable strength.
t.6.31.40: The sky seemed completely filled and the earth seemed wholly covered by the monkeys who had encamped around Laṅkā and by those still rushing toward it.
t.6.31.41: Others, a hundred hundred-thousands of bears and forest-dwelling monkeys, each in separate bands, approached the gates of Laṅkā from all sides to fight.
t.6.31.42: That mountain was surrounded on every side by all those monkeys, and a thousand times ten thousand of them advanced upon that city.
t.6.31.43: Surrounded on all sides by mighty monkeys with trees in their hands, Laṅkā became hard to enter even for the wind.
t.6.31.44: The Rākṣasas, suddenly hard pressed by the Vānaras, who resembled clouds and whose valour equalled Śakra's, were struck with astonishment.
t.6.31.45: A great sound arose there from that flood of troops as it advanced, like the roar of waters that would come from the ocean when it has burst its bounds.
t.6.31.46: By that mighty sound the whole of Laṅkā was shaken, together with its ramparts and arched gateways, its hills, woods and groves.
t.6.31.47: That army, protected by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and by Sugrīva, became all the more unassailable even by all the gods and asuras together.
t.6.31.48: Having thus stationed his own army for the slaying of the rākṣasas, Rāghava took counsel together with his ministers and made his resolve again and again.
t.6.31.49: Wishing to take the next step, and knowing the true purpose of acting in proper sequence, he, with Vibhīṣaṇa's approval and mindful of the duty of kings, summoned Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, and said this.
t.6.31.50: O gentle monkey, cross into the city of Laṅkā, cast off fear, and, free from distress, go to Daśagrīva and speak to him with my words.
t.6.31.51: O you whose splendor has fallen and whose sovereignty is gone, you who are bent on death and bereft of your senses! Of the sages and the gods, and likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases...
t.6.31.52: O night-wanderer, O Rākṣasa, whatever sin has been committed out of delusion by you, puffed up with arrogance, against the Nāgas, the Yakṣas and the kings...
t.6.31.53: Surely today your pride, born of the boon granted by Svayambhū, is gone, for I, tormented by the abduction of my wife, am the bearer of the rod of punishment for you. Holding that rod, I stand stationed at the gate of Laṅkā.
t.6.31.54: Slain by me, O Rākṣasa, you will go the way of the gods, of the great sages, and of all the royal sages.
t.6.31.55: O vilest of rākṣasas, show now that strength by which, having drawn me away through illusion, you carried off Sītā.
t.6.31.57: This Vibhīṣaṇa who has arrived is righteous of soul, the foremost of the Rākṣasas. This glorious one will surely attain the sovereignty of Laṅkā, free of all thorns.
t.6.31.56: With my sharpened arrows I shall rid this world of rākṣasas, unless you come to me for refuge, bringing Maithilī with you.
t.6.31.58: Indeed, the kingdom cannot be enjoyed by you through unrighteousness even for a moment, sinful as you are, with fools for your companions and a self that is unsubdued.
t.6.31.59: Or else, O Rākṣasa, summon up your resolve and, relying on your valor, fight. Laid to rest in battle by my arrows, you will then be purified.
t.6.31.60: Even if you enter the three worlds, having become a bird swift as thought, once you have come within the path of my sight you will not return alive.
t.6.31.61: I speak to you words for your own good: let your funeral rites be performed, and let Laṅkā be well looked upon, for your life now rests in my hands.
t.6.31.62: Thus addressed by Rāma, whose deeds were effortless, the son of Tārā rose into the sky and went forth like the fire-god Havyavāṭ in bodily form.
t.6.31.63: Flying swiftly in a moment to Rāvaṇa's palace, the glorious one saw Rāvaṇa seated there, unperturbed, together with his ministers.
t.6.31.64: Then, alighting not far from him, Aṅgada, the bull among monkeys, adorned with golden armlets, stood there like a blazing fire.
t.6.31.66: I am the messenger of Rāma, lord of Kosala, whose deeds are untiring; I am the son of Vālin, Aṅgada by name, if that name has ever reached your ears.
t.6.31.65: Having announced himself on his own, he made the king, together with his ministers, hear that entire excellent message of Rāma, with nothing left out and nothing added.
t.6.31.67: Rāma, the scion of Raghu, who increases the joy of Kausalyā, says to you: "Come forth and fight back, O cruel one, O vilest of men!"
t.6.31.68: I shall slay you together with your ministers, your sons, your kinsmen and your relatives; when you are slain, the three worlds will be free from fear.
t.6.31.69: Today I shall root out you, the enemy of the Devas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Uragas and Rākṣasas, and the thorn of the Ṛṣis.
t.6.31.70: And when you are slain, the sovereignty will pass to Vibhīṣaṇa, if you do not honour Vaidehī, bow down, and give her back.
t.6.31.71: As that bull among monkeys spoke such harsh words, the lord of the hosts of night-wanderers fell into the grip of fury.
t.6.31.72: Then he, his eyes copper-red with rage, commanded his ministers again and again: "Let this fool be seized! Let him be killed!"
t.6.31.73: Hearing the words of Rāvaṇa, whose splendour equalled a blazing fire, four fearsome night-rangers then seized him.
t.6.31.74: Then the heroic son of Tārā, of his own accord, deliberately let himself be seized, so that he might display his strength amid the host of Yātudhānas.
t.6.31.75: Then Aṅgada, taking up those who clung to his two arms as if they were birds, leapt up onto the palace that resembled a mountain.
t.6.31.76: Shaken from the sky by his force, those rākṣasas all fell to the ground while the lord of the rākṣasas looked on.
t.6.31.78: Having shattered the pinnacle of the palace and proclaimed his own name, he let out a mighty roar and flew up into the sky.
t.6.31.77: Then that palace pinnacle, lofty like a mountain peak, split apart under his tread as Daśagrīva looked on.
t.6.31.79: Rāvaṇa, for his part, became exceedingly wrathful at the violation of his palace, and, foreseeing his own destruction, he was given over wholly to sighing.
t.6.31.81: And Suṣeṇa, the monkey of great prowess, resembling a mountain peak, stood there surrounded by many monkeys able to assume any form at will.
t.6.31.82: At Sugrīva's command, the invincible monkey went round all four gates, as the moon moves among the stars.
t.6.31.83: Having observed a hundred akṣauhiṇīs of those forest-dwellers, who had crossed the ocean and encamped before Laṅkā,
t.6.31.84: Some rākṣasas were filled with amazement, and others likewise were seized with fear; still others, from their eagerness for battle, grew bold and daring.
t.6.31.85: The dejected rākṣasas saw the entire space between the rampart and the moat filled with monkeys, and the rampart itself turned into a wall of monkeys.
t.6.31.86: When that most terrifying uproar had arisen in the capital of the rākṣasa king, the rākṣasas, seizing their mighty weapons, rushed about like the winds at the end of a world-age.
t.6.31.80: But Rāma, surrounded by many joyful, roaring monkeys and longing to slay his enemy, advanced for battle itself.
